Midway through this semester, I applied for a ten-day field trip under the guise of "Field Investigation of Chang'an Sorcery." In Chang'an, I witnessed the sorcery practice of the target, Kong Kong'er.
It should be noted that all data in this report comes from long-distance visual observation, hearsay from street storytellers, and my own stress-induced memories from when I was almost caught by the target. Since the target refused to cooperate with academic interviews (and I have no intention of contacting such a dangerous individual), all inferences below are purely professional fabrication. Any similarities are purely coincidental and suggest that Kong Kong'er is indeed operating according to these principles.

I. Observation Records:
● Phenomenon A: "Three Immortals Return to the Cave" and Physical Manifestation of Clones
During combat, the target frequently creates physical clones identical to himself. These are not traditional illusionary projections—they can withstand attacks and even trigger mana resonance. Most bizarrely, the target can instantly swap positions between two clones, and the state of the original and the clone (including injury levels, residual mana, and even the folds in their clothing) seems to be synchronized during the swap.

● Phenomenon B: "Trickster's Hand" and Equipment Theft
 the target can snatch items from others out of thin air and transfer them to a third party or location. This process ignores physical distance and even whether the stolen item is currently in use.
I once witnessed a fully armed Chang'an security officer lose his gauntlet in the blink of an eye, and that gauntlet appeared in a passerby's hand the next second. Even more absurdly, when the target used this technique on the same person a second time, he returned the equipment—but the damage had already been done.

● Phenomenon C: "Gyro-Stabilization" and Spatial Vortices during Spellcasting
After unleashing his sorcery, the target enters a high-speed spinning state, simultaneously releasing clones and pulling in surrounding enemies. What puzzles me most is—why doesn't he get dizzy while spinning?
My multiple simulations in a safe area (the academy classroom) failed. The target's rotation is clearly not a simple physical movement, but a self-reconstruction of the spatial coordinate system—perhaps in his frame of reference, he isn't moving at all, and the whole world is spinning around him?

Preliminary Guess: This is by no means a simple mirror-copying technique. I suspect the target has mastered a "Parallel Self-Extraction in Folded Space" technique—temporarily pulling two counterparts from adjacent planes who might be doing the same action into the current reality. The essence of the position swap is the main consciousness jumping between bodies in different planes. The essence of his sorcery is related to the concept of space.

II. Conclusion:
 The core of ancient stage magic lies in "misdirection," or "attention guidance."
I boldly speculate that the target did not truly steal the equipment, but briefly "rewrote" the ownership of the equipment at the reality level. When the target performed it the first time, he tampered with the reality of "who holds the equipment"; when he performed it the second time, the causal rigidity of reality forced the item to return to its owner, but the damage, as "reality caused by sorcery," had already become a fact.
Its essence may be a spatial vortex generation technique with himself as the axis. The rotation is a visual persistence; in reality, the target is constantly tearing and reorganizing the surrounding spatial grid in an extremely short time, forcing enemies to slide toward the "point of lowest spatial density" (the target's location). The automatically released clones are the materialization of spatial turbulence generated at the edge of the vortex.

In summary, I can confirm:
Kong Kong'er's sorcery system is indeed built on the foundation of space-based sorcery. His clones, swapping, and equipment transfer all involve conventional sorcery operations on spatial dimensions.
However, "spatial" is only the surface-level answer. Beneath this, there is another layer of mechanism we have yet to understand—it weaves the "misdirection" philosophy of ancient stage magic, some unknown cursed energy, and especially the emotional memory energy related to that hand puppet, into a complex spell that cannot be fully parsed by existing sorcery theory.
Perhaps, as the target himself said: It's just a trick; it's boring once you see through it.

At the end of this report, I would like to quote an important document that I might write in the future:
"The most brilliant spatial spell is not making objects disappear, but making 'reality' itself questionable."
— "A Study of Magic in the Land of Kings"

They say the legends of Guye all revolve around those three divine swords. Let me tell you the tale today—whether it's true or false, there's no need to dwell on it.
Now, who hasn't heard of the Guye divine swords? The first is Frost, the second is Firmament, and the third is—World's End. They were forged by the Ancestor of Cloud-Casting, who gathered the essence of Cloud Stones and condensed the Razor Chill of cloud currents, taking three years of winter and summer to shape them. On the day the swords were completed, three claps of thunder rang out from thin air. Within the Reed Flower Grove, pillars of light shot into the clouds. Rumor in the martial world spread: "He who obtains the divine swords shall rule the world." Thus, heroes from all directions and titans from across the seas gathered before the Cloud-Casting Hut, eager to claim the legendary weapons.
As the light pillars faded, the truth was revealed—when the Frost sword was forged, snow fell in the summer outside the hut, its sword aura freezing everything for a thousand miles; when the Firmament sword emerged, its sword wind parted the clouds and the sun, its blade light capable of cleaving gold and stone; but when the World's End sword appeared, it was as red as blood mist, its blade light soul-snatching and maddening.
Heroes of Guye arrived, hearing the news, but taking the weapons was easier said than done.
A burly, bearded man stepped forward, eight feet tall, with the build of a tiger. Confident in his immense strength, he reached for Frost. He could still walk despite the ice, and he could break through the freezing, truly living up to his reputation for immense strength.
As he broke through the ice and finally gripped the hilt of Frost, he boasted: "With Frost in hand, I shall make the world bow." But in an instant, his blood froze, his right arm became as brittle as glass, and the ice spread through his veins until his whole body was frozen. With a "crack," he shattered into dust!
Then came a swordsman in white, with peerless lightness skills, drifting in to claim Firmament. The sword aura of Firmament filled the air for dozens of meters, continuous and unending. The swordsman in white seemed to walk on the wind, weaving through the sword gusts like flowing water, moving like a serpent.
Finally, his fingertips brushed the spine of Firmament. He stared at the heroes from all sides and declared: "This divine sword can only be mine." With that, he prepared to slaughter, but suddenly, the sound of clashing metal rang out. The swordsman in white looked down to see countless fine marks appearing on his hands, and a thousand bloodstains erupted across his body, as if he had been sliced to ribbons, leaving him battered and bruised before he collapsed to the ground.
Everyone sighed: "The formless sword aura of this blade strikes without a trace!"
Everyone was horrified: "The divine weapons choose their masters; we must reconsider." But then, the evil light of World's End flashed, and the experts felt their hearts in turmoil. Yet one man, a Tigerhead demon, with blood-red eyes and fur that seemed to drip with blood, boasted shamelessly: "This blood light is nothing. I feed on fur and drink blood; such bloodthirst is meant for me!"
He strolled forward, walking through the blood-red light with ease. The other heroes, seeing this, were naturally tempted and rushed forward, but merely touching the blood-red light left them restless and unable to proceed. The Tigerhead demon gripped World's End, looking invincible. A moment later, blood tears streamed from his red eyes, he could no longer speak, and he sank into a blood-lusting frenzy, slashing wildly with the sword. No one within the red light was spared, and finally, he cut his own throat and died.
When the sharpness of the three divine swords subsided, no one dared approach. Only the Ancestor of Cloud-Casting placed the divine swords away, enshrining them in the inner Cloud-Casting Hut, waiting for their true masters to arrive. The story of the divine swords spread like wildfire. Whether it was a woodcutter at the foot of the mountain, traveling merchants, or those in teahouses and taverns, everyone whispered—the Guye divine swords are impossible to tame, yet they can conquer the world.
Though the fame of the Guye divine swords spread across the four seas, human hearts are unpredictable, and greed never dies. Occasionally, uninvited guests would attempt to steal the swords.
That night, the moon was dark and the wind was high, with black clouds obscuring the sun. A shadow, like a ghost or a phantom, drifted in. There were no guards in the Cloud-Casting Hut, and the shadow felt a surge of joy, easily sneaking into the inner sanctum to see the three divine swords on display. The shadow looked around, confirming no one was there, and thought to himself: "The world says the divine swords choose their masters, but I don't believe in such nonsense! If I steal these three swords today, who in the world can challenge me?"
However, before he could even touch the divine swords, the shadow was struck by the backlash of the sword aura and was twisted beyond recognition. After this, no one dared to offend them again, and the martial world says: "Better to go to the underworld than to steal the divine swords."
To know who the divine weapons will choose, stay tuned for the next chapter!

The legend of the "Valor Ape" still circulates on Mount Guye. They say the monkey is pure silver-white and leaves no tracks in the snow. One moment it's catching fish in the mountain stream, and the next, it's resting in the shade at the peak.

There is only one person in this world who can match the Valor Ape in speed. No one knows their name, only catching glimpses of a white-clad, sword-bearing figure flashing through the bamboo forest.

Swordsman and ape, both unmatched in agility—but who is truly superior?

Thus, a race was born. The swordsman and the Valor Ape met in the bamboo forest at sunrise. Without a word, they both leaped like hawks into the bamboo.

The ape's arms were like lightning; with a few swings, it had traveled miles, vanishing into the shadows.

Just as the swordsman prepared to use his movement technique, he saw a tall, silver-haired figure holding a sword strolling through the bamboo. The swordsman hesitated, then stopped to pay his respects.

"Is this Master Alata?"

"It is."

The swordsman's heart stirred. Could Master Alata have come for the race between him and the Valor Ape?

"Master, why have you come to this bamboo forest?"

"To admire the bamboo."

"Do you not know that I am racing that ape here today?"

"What does the speed of one's movement matter?"

"The speed of movement..."

The swordsman was speechless for a moment, then bowed to Master Alata and leaped away.

When he reached the other side of the forest, the Valor Ape had been waiting for a long time. It chattered happily at his arrival, its pride evident.

But the swordsman didn't feel annoyed. He stared at the Valor Ape for a long time, until it began to bare its teeth in discomfort, and then he smiled.

"Brother Monkey, congratulations on the win. Want to go have a drink to celebrate? My treat."

"Chee?"

And so began the story of the man and the ape that would soon become famous across Mount Guye.

As the story goes, Fengxi bid farewell to his master and set out with his sword to roam the world. From then on, he championed the righteous, aided the needy, and punished the wicked. His name shook Mount Guye, and even the common folk knew of his chivalry. Wherever he and his monkey companion went, they were known to all.
However, good times did not last. The Chaoge army invaded, led by the 'General of Black Wind,' who set his sights on Mount Guye. With over a thousand troops, he sought to seize the three sacred swords protecting the mountain. Grandmaster Alata stood alone against them, battling the General for ten days and ten nights. Their black and white sword qi clashed, and amidst a hail of stones and arrows, Alata repelled the General. Yet, outnumbered and alone, he was left severely wounded despite his victory. The Chaoge army did not relent, immediately surrounding Mount Guye to force the mountain folk to surrender the sacred swords.
Learning of this, Fengxi rushed to his master's side, only to find Alata sitting in the bamboo forest, holding his breath and gathering his flow, murmuring only: 'I swear to protect the sacred swords and preserve the world.' Fengxi was troubled. On the day he was gifted the sword Pojun, he had sworn an oath to protect the blades. Now that Mount Guye was besieged, he had to take a desperate gamble to break the encirclement. Fengxi turned and left, whispering a plea for his master's forgiveness.
Determined, Fengxi and the Old White Ape charged straight into the enemy lines. Just as they broke through the mountain pass, they encountered two familiar faces—his foster siblings. It was a rare reunion, but with a great enemy at the gates, there was no time for pleasantries. The siblings offered their swords—the sacred swords of Mount Guye, forged by them together: the first, Frost, whose sword qi could freeze the sun; the second, Firmament, whose edge could pierce the heavens. Combined with the Pojun in Fengxi's hand, which could scatter armies with a single swing.

'Three swords united, the demon lord shall fall.'

Fengxi carried the three sacred swords and charged toward the enemy camp, accompanied by the Old White Ape, who ignored Fengxi's warnings, swearing to face the enemy together. The General of Black Wind appeared, his face hideous, wreathed in black energy. As the Chaoge soldiers gathered, a dark, mysterious flow converged, and in an instant, black mist filled the air, accompanied by ghostly wails.
Fengxi swung the Pojun, and the mist parted before his blade. He then swung Frost, condensing the mist and driving it back. As he danced with the Firmament sword, the black mist was replaced by a bloody haze. Seeing the tide turn, the General of Black Wind took to the field himself, summoning winds and rain, driving ghosts and spirits. Though Fengxi was brave, the dark arts were hard to break, and the loyal White Ape was defeated.
Seeing the General of Black Wind reach for the sacred swords, it seemed the fall of Mount Guye was imminent.

Fengxi remained silent, secretly channeling his inner energy to resonate with the Pojun. Man and sword became one, the sword wind biting. Fengxi transformed his body into a blade, flames erupting around him like a phoenix reborn. The General of Black Wind unleashed a wicked gale, but was forced to retreat by the flames—flames that were surely consuming Fengxi's own life force.
As the flames dimmed, the General of Black Wind was heavily wounded, yet the danger to Mount Guye remained. Fengxi, nearing exhaustion but unwilling to give up, channeled his flow into the sword. Forcing his power, blood surged and fused with the Pojun. The blade turned crimson. With a single slash, he created a blood-red barrier, sealing the General and his remaining troops within. The blood-red light collapsed in an instant, leaving only the Pojun standing in the earth, glowing with a sinister light. Its appearance had changed, and the onlookers were horrified, mistaking the blood-stained Pojun for the evil sword of the apocalypse.

The Old White Ape, desperate to save its master, rushed into the blood-red sword qi. Despite being torn to shreds, it sought to fulfill Fengxi's final wish—to return the sacred sword to Mount Guye. Alas, corrupted by the blood energy, it could no longer speak. A craftsman pointed to the sky and cursed: 'That Fengxi betrayed us, taking the sacred sword to beg for his life! It was only thanks to the loyal Old White Ape that the sword was recovered!' The loyal ape had no voice to argue, and consumed by the evil flow, it fled, never to be seen again.

Before they could grieve or mourn the Old White Ape, the 'apocalypse' sword emitted an evil flow, as if accusing Fengxi of his betrayal. The people of Mount Guye, unable to discern the truth, built the 'Atonement Rock,' carving inscriptions to condemn him, forcing generations to make Fengxi repent there to suppress the evil flow.

How tragic. Fengxi was a hero who sacrificed himself to protect Mount Guye. After his death, he suffered such unjust slander, his reputation destroyed. A loyal soul filled with resentment, even his name forbidden to be spoken.

Now that the hero is gone and his name tarnished, why do I, the writer, believe in Fengxi's innocence? Because I was once captured by the Sha-Wolves and saved by Fengxi. He was never one to fear death or cling to life; how could he have surrendered the sword to save himself? Thus, I write this to clear Fengxi's name, hoping his heroic spirit may find some solace.

"I know Nan Hulai, the genius raised in the Casting Cloud Hut." 
"We don't know where the genius is, but the Cloud-Mist weapons he makes are worth a fortune when sold to our market. But we also know that the Casting Cloud Hut guards against us like thieves, so how could his weapons be sold here?" 
"Brother Hu, aren't we thieves?" 
"Don't talk nonsense! You seem smart, so I'll tell you a bit more, don't talk blindly. Anyway, when the auction started that day, oh, what a scene, even many people from Chang'an came! As soon as that weapon appeared, there was a gasp from below—" 
"What, sword energy across the autumn?" 
"You have quite a vocabulary, kid. There wasn't a trace of hammering on the blade. From the blade to the hilt, it looked natural. From a distance, it was the color of the sky on the High Sky Cloud Cliff, and up close—it was like holding the cloud flow in your hand!" 
"Who could get close to see such a good thing?" 
"I heard it from someone who was there. At that time, the eyes of the people below were fixed on it. Before Bai Shouling could speak, they started bidding. The price increases came one after another, like waves. Our Sister Ling couldn't even keep up and barely managed to control the situation. Several people fought for a long time. One of them looked like he was about to lose, and the pull ring he was holding was about to loosen, but he was still hooking it with his finger, refusing to let go." 
"Does letting go of the pull ring mean giving up the bid?" 
"Yes, but that's all he had in his pocket, what else could he do? The customer was staring at the Cloud-Mist weapon, sweating profusely, his eyes red. Continue bidding? He didn't have a penny left. Give up bidding? The person opposite also looked like he was at the end of his rope, maybe if he added a little more, he would have succeeded!" 
"Brother Hu, don't we have those brothers who handle on-site credit for people? Why didn't they go up and talk at a time like this?" 
"That's right, Abacus Old Jia went up in three steps, asking how much the customer wanted to borrow. But the customer was in a dilemma. He didn't have anything decent to mortgage, so he just gritted his teeth and pushed his daughter out." 
"He even mortgaged his daughter?" 
"The Cloud-Mist weapon was about to be in his hands, the customer was anxious, what else was in his eyes? Old Jia said the little girl didn't really know what was happening and was foolishly about to follow him—hey, at this moment, Lu Cang rushed out." 
"What does she have to do with it?" 
"Old Jia was also puzzled. He saw Lu Cang wearing white clothes—you know, they don't wear our skin in Chenshi, they dress like decent people all day, really taking themselves for good people—walked straight to the customer, holding the little girl with one hand and the customer with the other, whispering in the customer's ear for a long time, and then the deal was done!" 
"Did she threaten the customer with the little girl?" 
"How is that possible? But after she finished talking, the customer loosened the pull ring and turned to open the order with her. I think she has the life to open that order but not the life to take it. Hmph, you just wait for her to come back and cry to us in a couple of days." 
"That's not right, Brother Hu, wasn't that a big order?" 
"You only know it's big, do you know what that order is for? Lu Cang boasted that she could get Nan Hulai's next weapon for half the price, as long as the customer didn't mortgage his daughter. Don't you think she's just blowing smoke?" 
"Oh, she's just shooting herself in the foot! But what is she trying to get out of this order?" 
"Who knows? She is most famous for being able to grind. She works silently all day, afraid of not grinding us to death. But this time she took the order, it was indeed suspicious... Have time to check her at the workshop archives!" 
"Hey Brother Hu, now that you mention it, I have an impression. Didn't Lu Cang get sold by her father when she first came to our market!" 
"I really haven't heard of this, tell me in detail." 
"Back then, Lu Cang's father took a fancy to a Cloud-Mist weapon with good quality. He was short of the last bit of money, so he mortgaged her here, saying he was going home to get the money, and then he never came back. Brother Hu, do you think the weapon in his hand was too flashy and he was targeted and robbed on the way?" 
"Maybe it's true. No wonder she's working so hard, maybe she's earning money for her own redemption. With the little money we have, she'll have to earn until the Year of the Monkey. But she doesn't earn much from this order, what is she after... that little girl? Does she really take herself for a good person? There's no one with a clean background here... Forget it, forget it, talked for so long, pour the tea!"

A Guye tale often speaks of the three divine swords, linked either to the cloud-casting or to the great chaos.
However, there remains a wandering hero who holds the fourth divine sword. This untold story, I shall now recount for you all.

Everyone knows the bamboo forest of Guye, but few know that a strange magical species lives within it. It is said that their descendants are never born in winter.
Yet, a woman was pregnant for several years, which was already against the norm, and it just so happened that on the day of the beginning of winter, she went into labor and gave birth to a child. The clansmen were all disgusted. When this child was born, there were no strange celestial phenomena or auspicious signs, but the clan elders secretly thought: "A child born in winter must be an omen of misfortune. If we keep this child, it may bring disaster upon the clan." After much deliberation, they decided to abandon him.
That night, the first snow fell, dusting the green with white. The father held the infant and placed him under the bamboo. Everything was silent, save for the sound of snow falling on bamboo leaves. The child did not cry; his breathing was as thin as a thread, like a dying breeze.
Just then, a craftsman cutting bamboo passed by and saw the swaddled infant under the bamboo. He approached and saw it was a baby. This child was not meant to die; it was fate, and he would surely achieve great things in the future. He took him home and raised him with care. Thinking his breathing was as shallow as the wind, he wanted to name him—but his true name cannot be spoken. If written down, this book might never see the light of day, so he is temporarily called "Bamboo-Born," to record his origins.
Bamboo-Born was naturally gifted. By the age of seven or eight, he could identify gold ore, help his foster father forge swords, and help his foster mother control fire.
His foster parents had a son and a daughter of similar age, and they grew up together like siblings. Bamboo-Born was attached to the bamboo forest, his soul lingering there. Whenever he had free time, he would wander through it, either leaning against the bamboo in thought or plucking leaves to play the flute, as if he had infinite worries he wanted to confide to the wind among the bamboo.
One day, there was a rustling of sword wind in the forest. Looking up, he saw someone dancing with a sword in the depths. The sword passed without harming the bamboo leaves, and the steps moved without raising dust. With a burst of power, the sword energy was like a rainbow. Seeing this, Bamboo-Born casually plucked a bamboo leaf and spun to parry, actually managing to Negate the sword energy.
The sword dancer walked over; it was none other than Master Alata. Master Alata looked around the bamboo forest, sighed at his talent, and wanted to take Bamboo-Born as his disciple, bestowing upon him the name Fengxi.
Fengxi had high comprehension; he understood sword moves at a hint and grasped sword principles at a teaching. Within three years, he had obtained Alata's true inheritance. Fengxi thought to himself: "Now that my swordsmanship is complete, I should not stay under others' care any longer and add to my foster parents' worries." He decided to bid farewell and venture into Guye.
At the moment of parting, Alata was silent for a long time before slowly speaking: "Having ambitions for the world is a good thing, but no matter where your sword points, you must protect the peace of Guye." Alata nodded and took out a sword, handing it to Fengxi. This sword was named "Breaker of Armies." When the sword was drawn, the wind whistled; when it passed, the wind broke. This was one of the three divine swords of Guye, which had been hidden by Alata all along.
With the sword passed to Fengxi, Alata must have had high hopes for this child. The name Fengxi would surely shake Guye.

One day, Fengxi passed by an old mountain head and suddenly heard crying and shouting from the forest. Listening intently, it was the wailing of women and the crying of children.
Fengxi followed the sound, moving silently without wind. Seeing the full picture of the forest, it was a bandit stronghold plundering women and children. Fengxi was furious, thinking that such evil bandits causing chaos in Guye could not be left alone.
With that, he drew his sword and stepped forward, heading straight for the bandit lair. The bandit leader, seeing that Fengxi was only one person, couldn't help but sneer, wanting to duel Fengxi one-on-one. The Breaker of Armies was drawn, the stance was set, and Fengxi offered to let the bandit leader have three moves. The bandit leader, never having suffered such humiliation, slashed wildly with his blade, kicking up dust and shattering boulders—he was that fierce.
After the bandit leader's three moves, he was terrified. Fengxi was nowhere to be seen, hidden in the dust. Only a cold flash was seen, and the sword tip pointed straight at the bandit leader's throat. The bandit leader raised his blade to block, but the steel blade shattered instantly. The bandit leader retreated, barely avoiding the sword edge, but unarmed and desperate, he shouted for the bandits in the lair to surround and attack.
Fengxi remained calm. Among the bandits, his sword danced like a flower, and blood fell like rain. His dance steps were elegant, with the grace of Alata, playing among the bandits. The Breaker of Armies was like the wind, blowing to the bandit leader's throat. The wind stopped, and the bandit leader stared, his accomplices all dead. The sword wind stirred slightly, and only the sound of dripping blood remained; the bandit lair was silent. Fengxi cut the chains with his sword, and everyone was saved. The women and children knelt and thanked him, weeping. Fengxi went deep into the bandit lair and found an iron cage with a monkey locked inside, looking quite ordinary.
Seeing this, Fengxi was moved, his situation just like his own as Bamboo-Born. He couldn't help but be touched and wanted to set it free, naming it White Ape Elder.
Who would have thought that this monkey could speak human language? From then on, it was inseparable, following Fengxi everywhere. One man and one monkey, venturing through Guye. To know what happens next, wait for the next installment.

Back to the traitor who stole the swords. That night, dark clouds obscured the moon, concealing a murderous intent, until suddenly the clouds parted and the moon shone bright. Everyone stared in shock—it was the Demon-kind swordsman, wielding three divine swords! The heroes of Guye were all horrified. With such skill and divine weapons in hand, who could stop him? The other two sword masters had already lost their blades, their fates uncertain. A deathly silence fell, broken only by the wailing wind, as if Guye itself were mourning.
"Villain, leave the divine swords behind!" With a thunderous roar, a figure leaped out like an ape, fast as lightning and swift as a shooting star, blocking the traitor's path. The man's face was covered in fur, making his true features hard to discern, but his eyes burned like torches. Later generations would call him the Fur-Faced Righteous Warrior.
Before the warrior could react, the traitor brandished Frost, and instantly, a chill erupted, freezing the ground three feet deep and coating the vegetation in frost. The warrior moved as if flying, treading across the ice. While the surface was too slick for ordinary men to stand, the warrior walked as if on flat ground. He reached the traitor and smashed his fist into the ground, the force of his blow shattering the ice.
The traitor then brandished Firmament, and sword energy rained down like a dense storm. The Fur-Faced Warrior plucked a tuft of fur and flung it with all his might. The fur transformed into a rain of needles, and wherever it passed, the sword energy dissipated without a sound.
Then, a flash of blood-red lightning struck. The warrior charged headlong, ignoring the blood spraying from a deep gash in his chest, and landed a backhanded punch squarely on the traitor's chest. Though severely wounded, the warrior's punch was so powerful that the traitor was sent reeling, causing him to drop both Frost and Firmament.
Seeing this, the people of Guye whispered, "The traitor must be unjust, and the divine swords have rejected him. This Fur-Faced Warrior must be the incarnation of the divine swords themselves to command such power."
Suddenly, the evil energy of the end times surged. The traitor was enveloped in a bloody glow, his eyes burning red like blood, appearing as if possessed by madness. Just then, an arrow pierced his heart. The swordsman froze, looking down to see the arrowhead protruding from his chest, blood gushing out. It was the enemy general from Zhaoge, who had acted with treachery, waiting for the traitor to steal the swords before stabbing him in the back. The Zhaoge general sneered, "You are no longer the sword master; what use are you? It is clear now that divine swords can change owners, and you have become a burden!"
The enemy general led his troops to seize the swords, but the warrior struggled to his feet and picked up Frost and Firmament. In his hands, they resonated, their sword energy piercing the heavens. With a mere wave, he unleashed a force capable of breaking armies, wiping out the thousands of soldiers! Yet, even after the army was destroyed, remnants remained, not to mention the Zhaoge general. By then, the Fur-Faced Warrior was at his last breath, unable to fight further.
The traitor looked up and laughed bitterly, hating Zhaoge for their treachery and himself for his betrayal. The blood-red energy of the end times spread with his hatred, overflowing into a blood mist that shrouded the Zhaoge general, his remnants, the warrior, and the traitor himself. Wherever the mist touched, the Zhaoge soldiers' eyes turned red, and they slaughtered each other; even the Zhaoge general gouged out his own eyes.
The traitor, holding the End-Times sword, swayed unsteadily. With his hatred undiminished and his regret unrecognizable, he had long since lost his mind. He raised his sword to strike the warrior, who raised his own to block. As the blades clashed, sparks flew, and suddenly a beam of light shot into the sky, dispersing the blood mist. When the dust settled, both the Fur-Faced Warrior and the divine swords had vanished without a trace, leaving only the traitor's corpse.
As for that corpse, it cracked inch by inch, and a bloody light shot into the sky, solidifying into a massive, dark-red boulder! Around the boulder, vegetation withered, and birds and beasts that flew over it would fall dead. If one were to approach it carelessly, they would bleed from their seven orifices within three days.
The malevolence grew daily, and the curse of sin spread. Fortunately, the craftsmen of the Casting Cloud Pavilion sacrificed their lives to carve the traitor's crimes onto the stone, hence it was named the "Atonement Rock." The people prayed day and night to suppress the evil, but the malice remained, so they placed a statue of the traitor before the rock to repent for eternity.
Some ask where the divine swords went, or who the warrior was, or if the Atonement Rock can suppress the evil forever. Rumors in Guye abound, but there is no conclusion. The legend of the divine swords ends here, but their fame shall endure forever.
The story ends here. The content is purely fictional, so do not take it to heart. Tales are always a mix of truth and falsehood, and the author takes no responsibility for them.

As mentioned before, the Long siblings received the true teachings of the Old Man of the Clouds, spreading the technique of quenching with cloud flow to many, calling it "Cloud-Mist." Within ten years, the "Cloud-Mist Weapons" became famous, and everyone in the martial world took pride in wielding one. Those who sought the swords found that they cut through iron like mud and sliced gold without a sound, sighing as they stroked the blades: "All the swords under heaven are not worth a third of Guxie's!"
With such fame, is it a blessing or a curse?
There was a notorious bandit named "Red Claw" who bought a Cloud-Mist blade with a heavy sum. This thief rampaged with the blade, committing seven massacres in a month, with nearly a hundred souls lost to his blade. The Aerwatch issued a bounty, but could not harm him in the slightest, losing dozens of men instead. This shook Guxie, and the Cloud-Casting Hut was in an uproar. Long Nian slammed the table: "The divine weapon is not at fault; it is the human heart that is evil! From today on, Cloud-Mist weapons will no longer be sold. Anyone seeking a weapon must pass the 'Three Heart-Questioning Trials' to prove their virtue." This became the predecessor to the current rules of the Cloud-Casting Hut.
However, when this rule was announced, the martial world was in an uproar. Some who truly sought the swords accepted the test, but others were angered, their demands for swords rejected, and they roared: "A tiny Cloud-Casting Hut, how dare you set rules?" They gathered bandits from nine mountain strongholds and eighteen gullies, intending to seize the Cloud-Mist weapons by force.
Bandits raided Guxie at night, torches like dragons. But before the mountain gate, a Demon-kind swordsman stood with his sword, his red hair dancing in the night wind. Before the End of Days was even drawn, the killing intent already filled the air. The bandit leader ordered a charge, and the Demon-kind let out a long howl. Sword light like a blood dragon emerging from the sea instantly cut down dozens of fierce bandits. Long Qi and Long Nian also arrived; the Firmament sword summoned bolts of lightning, and the Frost sword formed layers of ice walls. As the bandits fled, the thief gritted his teeth: "This debt will be repaid!"
Now, there was a general in Zhaoge who loved collecting divine weapons. The fleeing thief heard of this and sought an audience with the general, telling him of the power of the Guxie divine swords. The Zhaoge general's ambition flared: "If I can arm my three armies with such weapons, why worry that the world won't be mine?" He led fifty thousand elite troops, three thousand chariots, and eight thousand iron cavalry, marching straight toward Guxie. When their banners blocked the sun, they camped ten miles away, their lines like a long snake coiled around the mountain.
Looking down from the heights, the Long siblings saw the magnificent army and the killing intent rising to the heavens. Long Nian frowned: "If the divine weapons fall into Zhaoge's hands, the common people will suffer." Suddenly, inspiration struck, and she clapped her hands: "Why not use the mountain as a forge and the swords as a city?"
Immediately, the three scattered, each guarding a side. Long Qi held Firmament, climbed to the peak, and pointed his sword at the sky, drawing the cloud flow of the nine heavens to circle the mountain three times. The clouds condensed into substance, white as silk by day and silver gauze by night. Long Nian grasped Frost, stood by the cold pool, and pointed her sword at the rapids, summoning ten thousand feet of mysterious ice from the earth's veins. Ice walls rose layer by layer, ten feet high and three feet thick, shimmering with seven colors in the sunlight. The Demon-kind swordsman leaped to the mountain pass, and as his divine sword left its sheath, blood energy overflowed, forming a thousand-mile barrier of red mist. Within the mist, sword shadows flickered, and death lurked.
Seeing the strange phenomena in the mountains, the Zhaoge general sneered: "Playing tricks!" He ordered three thousand heavy infantry to advance. As they entered a hundred paces, the Frost sword aura turned the front hundred men and horses into ice statues in various poses. Advancing another fifty paces, the edge of the Firmament sword descended from the clouds, turning steel armor and iron helmets into powder, those struck as if hit by lightning. Where the blood energy spread, the rear soldiers' eyes turned red, and they began to slaughter each other.
Though they repelled the ten thousand troops, they were now trapped on a lonely mountain. Provisions would only last a month, and though the mountain spring had not run dry, a long siege would surely lead to defeat. The future remained uncertain; the three swords protecting the mountain were merely a stay of execution. More worrying was whether the disaster caused by the divine swords could be solved by the divine swords themselves?
Thus, the Cloud-Mist weapons brought disaster, the three swords formed a city to guard the lonely peak, and though the army was repelled, the trap remained.

Many years ago, my master told me there were only two kinds of people in this world: those who hurt others and those who save them. The Hundred Herbs family belonged to the latter.
I believed this deeply, until A'ao appeared.

The sudden rainy season in Jixia shrouded the world in a hazy mist.
That day, I had just become an apprentice of the Hundred Herbs family, following my master to gather herbs.
A wounded fawn caught my attention; its limping hind leg was bleeding profusely.
I followed it quietly until it collapsed from exhaustion, and only then did I notice an arrowhead embedded in its leg.
Just as I was wondering what to do, heavy footsteps sounded, and a pack of fierce beasts surrounded us.
My master had said that a pack of beasts had been roaming nearby, hurting many people, and that ordinary people in the wild were unlikely to survive an encounter with them.
I was scared and wanted to call for my master, but looking around, I realized I had strayed too far from him while following the fawn.
"I wonder, are your claws faster, or is my blade faster..."
It was a girl about my age, holding a wooden sword and standing between me and the beasts, mimicking the tone of an adult.
She was no match for the beasts.
Amidst the snarling, the girl suffered countless wounds, but she never gave up, gritting her teeth and facing the beasts with her broken wooden sword.
In the end, the sounds of the fight drew patrolling militia. The beasts were captured, and the fawn and the girl gradually recovered under my master's care.
I asked the girl why she saved me.
"I wasn't saving you. It's just... I want to be the strongest warrior on the continent. Have you ever seen a strong person run away and leave someone behind?"
"Then who is the strongest right now?"
"I don't know, but... once I defeat everyone stronger than me, I'll be the strongest."
"Why do you want to be the strongest?"
She looked at me and smiled, but didn't answer.
"My name is Yun Zhao, what's yours?"
"You don't need to know." She still pretended to be cold.
"You're so stubborn... I'll just call you A'ao. You can call me A'zhao."
Later, I learned she didn't like the nickname, always feeling it sounded like some kind of animal, but she had tacitly accepted it at the time.
From then on, I continued to study the Hundred Herbs, saving the injured people and animals before me. A'ao remained obsessed with martial arts, often ending up covered in wounds from training or duels, only to come to the pharmacy and let me treat her without a word.
One afternoon many years later, she came to say goodbye.
She had heard that the Northlands were full of martial arts sects and masters, and she wanted to go and make a name for herself.
I don't know why, but I wasn't surprised at all.
Before she left, I asked her when she would return. She stared at me, and it was a long time before she spoke.
"A'zhao."
"Hmm?"
"You asked me before why I wanted to be the strongest."
"I did ask."
"It's a pity..." she said mysteriously.
"Why?"
"If you came with me, you would definitely know the reason."
The cool autumn wind blew from afar again, carrying the familiar scent of loess.
A'ao was direct in a fight, but her words were always so circuitous.
I was moved by her words.
In the glow of the sunset, we walked one after the other through the swirling dust, A'ao's sleeves fluttering in the evening breeze.
I think my master wasn't entirely right. People can be divided into two types: the cruel who hurt others, and the compassionate who save them.
But in this vast world, there is always a third kind of person.

Long Wei, the seventh-generation master craftsman, though controversial, was undoubtedly the greatest sword smith of her time. Opinions on her were divided; some said she was wasteful, using all sorts of Common Skills to forge swords with high loss rates, while others claimed she ignored ancestral rules, arbitrarily changing forging methods and showing no respect for others. Yet, her notes clearly show that from quenching duration to the number of hammer strikes, every detail was for the sake of forging the ultimate sword. She was the most passionate master craftsman when it came to sword forging.
During Long Wei's tenure, she held the Sword Sacrifice ceremony seven times. For these seven ceremonies, seven sword blanks were forged using seven different furnace temperatures, never repeating. Using these seven swords as a benchmark, she recorded the reaction of Cloud-Accumulation Stone to temperature changes, from the start of softening to the end of shaping, leaving nothing out, and eventually creating a precise table. Since then, the Cloud-Flow weapon lineage has used this as the standard for temperature control with Cloud-Accumulation Stone; the success of this standardization is all thanks to her.
Every time Long Wei held a Sword Sacrifice, she would emerge with a broken sword, not only without anger but with eyes shining, walking with a spring in her step, her excitement evident. To her, the Sword Sacrifice was not about perfection, but about testing the limits of her craft—knowing where the sword broke revealed the flaw, and the appearance of the break revealed the temperature. What others saw as "failure" was the most precious data to her. Such a mindset is only possible for someone truly obsessed.
Long Wei forged countless swords in her life, but she left her proudest work—the broken sword of Chi Shang—in the Sword Sacrifice ceremony, never to be taken out again. The patterns on this sword were like a ruler, dense and precise, showing the rigor of the smith. Yet the interesting part is this: Long Wei, a person who used the most rigorous attitude, performed the boldest experiments. I suppose the choice of a master craftsman is something ordinary people cannot fathom.
……
During Long Sheng's tenure, he also held a Sword Sacrifice ceremony. In terms of forging ability, no one in Casting Cloud Pavilion could surpass him at the time, and even across the entire Guxie region, he was considered world-class. It is a pity that he was somewhat different from the master craftsmen of the past. Long Wei's obsession was with the sword itself—furnace temperature, texture, quenching duration—everything was pursued to the extreme, almost to the point of paranoia. Long Sheng was different. Since the rise of Sky-Light Workshop and the decline of Casting Cloud Pavilion, besides forging skills, management was also essential. Long Sheng took on this heavy responsibility amidst the difficulties. As a master craftsman, he studied how to secure orders and manage the pavilion. I suppose the duty of a master craftsman should not just be forging, it's just that previous generations did not have to face this so directly.
The sword he offered in the Sword Sacrifice ceremony was named "He Xu". The name of this sword alone reveals his state of mind—"How to continue?" is a question for the sword, for the pavilion, and for himself. Interestingly, the patterns on this sword look chaotic at first glance, but upon closer inspection, they have a sense of unity, as if there is order in chaos; the hardness of the sword is neither too rigid nor too soft, striking a balance. Everything is the way of the golden mean. The golden mean is not mediocrity. Just like Long Sheng himself, he was skilled but not arrogant, open to management but without losing his bottom line, seeking a glimmer of hope between tradition and change. He is worthy of the title of master craftsman.
……
Long Mu was supposed to be the contemporary master craftsman at the time of compilation, but an incident occurred, and he returned to the old site during the Sword Sacrifice ceremony. As I mentioned regarding Long Sheng, facing new impacts, the master craftsman Casting Cloud Pavilion needs is no longer the same as in the past. Although Long Mu's forging skills were excellent, they were not top-tier, but he was better at management and had served as Long Sheng's business consultant. Perhaps he understood better in what direction Casting Cloud Pavilion should develop to continue standing in Guxie. Unfortunately, he passed away young and could not see where the Casting Cloud Pavilion led by Long Mu would eventually go.
Long Xi, the current master craftsman and daughter of Long Mu, masters a special flow of cold. She studied under Long Sheng and was also influenced by her father to explore management. Long Mu's regrets may be made up for by Long Xi, leading Casting Cloud Pavilion in the direction Long Mu hoped for.
……

The moon is bright and the wind is clear, the first snow falls, and nameless birds chirp incessantly on the withered branches. A'ao stands before the lacquered red courtyard gate, sword in hand, her youthful brows showing determination. The gate opens. The young girl shakes the frost from her sleeves and strides into the courtyard. In the early winter many years ago, A'ao, having just mastered her swordsmanship, left her homeland and traveled thousands of miles to challenge the renowned Pijin Sect. There were only a few disciples in the courtyard, looking at her with surprise. "I want to spar with your sect leader," A'ao said. "Who are you? You think you can challenge our leader?" the disciples sneered. "Pardon the intrusion." A'ao gripped the hilt of her sword. By the time the Pijin Sect leader stepped out of the pavilion, the disciples were already lying on the ground, groaning in pain. The leader's eldest son, the future heir of the Pijin Sect, was among them. Her sword had not even been unsheathed. The leader set aside his anger and carefully examined the girl before him. She was no mere troublemaker. "A pleasure to meet you." "Likewise." The snow intensified, the night wind bit, and the melting snow on the eaves turned into icicles before it could fall. After a moment of silence, two cold, gleaming swords were drawn, sparks flying everywhere. A'ao held her sword with one hand and leaped up like a diving falcon. The leader held his breath, parrying methodically. Her sword light was like a gale, and where the sword shadow passed, the snow remained unmarked. The leader suddenly struck, his sword edge turning sharply, his moves like a collapsing glacier, heavy and powerful, each strike aimed at A'ao's openings. A'ao's moves had been seen through by the leader. Unable to dodge, A'ao was wounded by the blade and fell into the snow. Her hair tie was cut, her dark hair cascaded like a waterfall, and blood seeped from her forehead. "Shall we stop here?" The leader's respectful words carried a hint of contempt. The girl was indeed a martial arts talent, but her wings were not yet fully grown; her moves and temperament still needed polishing. "No need." A'ao wiped the blood from her forehead, swung her sword to cut off her own hair, and lunged forward like a desperate bird of prey. Their blades clashed, silver light illuminating the snowy night, the girl's figure weaving through the sword light like a passionate dancer. A'ao's sleeves were soaked with sweat, her sword momentum gradually slowing, but the leader was also exhausted, with many wounds. With a crisp sound, her sword was shattered by the leader. The Pijin Sect had always been famous for splitting stones and breaking gold. The leader did not intend to stop and rushed toward A'ao with his sword. In a flash, a cold edge pressed against the leader's throat. It was ice. She had pulled an icicle to use as a sword; if she hadn't stopped in time, the leader would have been in grave danger. "I won." The girl dropped the icicle and turned to leave. The dawn was still thin, and the morning wind blew through the valley. Yunzhao brought steaming medicinal herbs and helped A'ao up to take them. Within a year, after defeating the Pijin Sect, A'ao had challenged many famous sects one after another. Although her fame grew, she was often injured. "I heard the young master of the Pijin Sect is badly hurt and hasn't recovered yet..." Yunzhao muttered while preparing the medicine for her. "Then they can come and seek revenge," A'ao said lightly. "Must you walk this path?" "I am already on it." "You really are impossible... I shouldn't have followed you." "But you came anyway." A'ao laughed cheekily, and Yunzhao was amused as well. Their laughter flew out of the wooden house, over the mountains and forests, and echoed in the sky. "Winter is coming again," A'ao said softly, looking out the window. The grass and trees were withered, the wild geese were flying south, and the begonias by the stream stood against the wind. As autumn grew colder, all things that craved warmth had just bid farewell to the end of summer, only to endure the wind and frost. So too, do those who carry fire in their hearts.

Mad Snow Blade sneered three times, "Nanhu Lai, you won't be able to forge this sword." Nanhu Lai ignored him and continued fiddling with the Cloud-Accumulating Stone. The cut surface of the stone was clean and sharp, with wisps of cloud flowing faintly within—truly a top-tier ore. Mad Snow Blade tossed his sword onto the table with a crisp clatter; it was indeed a fine blade. "Listen to that sound, that is the true sound of a Cloud-Severing weapon. Now listen to what you've been forging these past few days; if you put it on an old lady's cutting board to crush garlic, she'd complain that your scrap metal is useless." Nanhu Lai still ignored him, his movements slowing down. "Stop pretending. You know full well that the quenching crack wasn't the fault of the ore, nor the furnace." "Nanhu Lai, the problem is in your heart." Mad Snow Blade dragged Nanhu Lai out of the Cloud-Forging Hut. The starry night was deep, and the wind pushed the Kongming lanterns of Wulian Town, guiding them both up to that dilapidated Red Maple Pavilion. "Why did you bring me here? It's not like my Sword Heart is unstable." As he said this, Nanhu Lai looked back at the flickering lights of Wulian Town. Mad Snow Blade studied Nanhu Lai, then pointed to the dim, indistinct mountains in the distance. "See that? Those dozens of trials you pointed at back then are all losers to Lu Cang now. She has already plucked the moon for you, but you know deep down that even so, she is not worthy of a Cloud-Severing weapon." Silence reigned. "Just say the word, and I can make sure she never bothers you again." The wind suddenly turned sharp. "It's my fault. I shouldn't have agreed to forge this sword if I didn't want to. Since I agreed, I'm now in a dilemma, but is sword-forging judged by one's actions or one's heart? When I agreed, I just thought of her as an ordinary bounty hunter. Driving away a sword-seeker who came for my reputation would be a loss for the Cloud-Forging Hut, so I intentionally made things difficult. But you know..." The wind softened again. "I know. People in the mountains say that anyone who can pass those trials is a hero with a Sword Heart. A bounty hunter can't have a Sword Heart; if they had even a shred of conscience, they couldn't survive in the Ruins Market." Mad Snow Blade waved his hand, drew his sword from its scabbard, and shoved it back in. Nanhu Lai remained silent. He opened his mouth slightly to argue, but the wind on the pavilion choked his words back. What could he say? It would just be a few empty platitudes about not judging a book by its cover, or some unbelievable excuses about being forced into it by the Light-Casting Workshop. "Asking you one more time, do you want my help?" "No need. This is a matter I must handle properly myself. I agreed to forge this sword, and I will bear the consequences of whatever method I use. Also, if Qingping goes to find you, don't promise her anything." Mad Snow Blade watched Nanhu Lai's figure disappear into the night and drew his sword again. A few drops of faded blood splattered on the hilt; he had been a bit too heavy-handed when he cut down those bounty hunters earlier. A pity, it was a good blade. "Qingping, stop wearing such a long face. Come tell your brother Jinglei what's going on, alright?" Mad Snow Blade leaned against the table, silent, quietly sharpening his blade. At the other end of the table, the great cause of the Jianghu had already begun to shine.
The finished and semi-finished products in the workshop are all finely crafted, with the cold gleam of the blades revealing the artisan's dedication.

Only one person remained on the arena stage.
For many days, she had been there.
It wasn't that she enjoyed standing at such heights, but rather that she was waiting for an opponent.
An opponent who could rival her.
At that time, the arena was not yet famous; only a few martial arts fanatics frequented it for sparring. No one could have imagined that it would later become a renowned holy site for duels in the North.
And a place becomes a holy site either because something extraordinary happened there, or because an extraordinary person appeared.
That day, people were sparring on the stage as usual, with a sparse crowd gathered around, discussing each other's moves.
As the daylight brightened, a strange figure appeared on the stage.
People could vaguely make out that she was a young girl, carrying a worn-out wooden sword, her expression listless.
There had been no rain recently, yet she still wore a bamboo hat and a straw cape.
Those on the stage, unsure of her intentions, stepped forward to ask.
She did not answer, simply pulling out her wooden sword and pointing it at the other, as if challenging them to a duel.
People were baffled by her posture, and after much discussion, they decided to let a beginner spar with her.
After all, she was just a girl with a broken wooden sword; playing along would suffice, as they feared hurting her if they took it seriously.
To everyone's surprise, before they could even blink, the beginner and his weapon were knocked off the stage.
No one saw how she struck, nor did anyone know why that wooden sword possessed such power.
People began to take it seriously, stepping onto the stage one after another, using their best techniques to challenge the girl, but they were defeated one by one.
A few days later, no one dared to challenge her anymore, and her reputation gradually spread far and wide.
Many martial artists, drawn by her name, traveled thousands of miles to see her. After witnessing her skills, some felt unwilling to accept defeat, some felt exhilarated, and others stayed to observe.
Until the first time she was defeated.
That swordsman's skill was not superior to the girl's, but when their weapons clashed, the girl's wooden sword snapped.
She stood frozen in place, staring at the broken sword, completely forgetting to dodge the opponent's moves.
She lost, and she was severely injured.

She woke up in a rocking boat.
Golden light shimmered on the river surface, and a fisherman at the bow rowed the oars, humming an unknown tune.
After losing the duel, she had left the arena. When she reached the bridge, her injuries flared up, and she fell into the river, only to be rescued by the fisherman who pulled her onto his boat.
Day after day, the girl insisted on leaving before she had fully recovered.
"You kept calling out for A-Zhao while you were unconscious," the fisherman said before they parted ways.
The girl lowered her head, wanting to say something but stopping.
"You were very close to A-Zhao, weren't you?" the fisherman asked.
"Yes... she liked to heal people or save small animals, but she didn't know how to protect herself. I used this wooden sword to save her before..." the girl said, looking at the broken sword in her arms.
"So it really was a wooden sword... I couldn't tell after it broke in two," the fisherman scratched his head.
"Broken wood is hard to mend; it can't be put back together."
"I've lived on a boat my whole life and know little of the land, but perhaps the two broken pieces will take root in different places."
"How is that possible... this wood rotted many years ago."
The fisherman shook his head, looking at the distant horizon.
"I don't know about your wood, but I've seen a tree that, even after being withered for a thousand years, will sprout new buds when it meets rain and sunlight."
The sunlight grew stronger. After the rainy season, the currents were swift, duckweed was lush, water birds were flying, and the boat drifted on the wide river.
Warm breezes lifted the girl's hair, and the broken wood creaked in her bag.
"That direction... is that Jixia?" she pointed toward the distant mountains.

Drawing a bucket of water from the well, clear of any impurities, she poured it into a copper kettle and set it over the fire. Guests at the forest tea stall are never in a hurry; the longer they sit, the more fresh stories they hear. The woman brewing the tea is in no rush either. She could easily fan the flames to make the water boil faster, but she just sits on her small stool, creaking back and forth, listening to the guests leisurely spinning their tales.
Today's story is much like this forest tea stall, set in a bamboo grove just like this one.
The guest carrying a sword spoke first, dipping a finger in tea to draw on the table. Others gathered around as he wrote a place name: Moon-Reflecting. It's not a famous scenic spot, known only to the locals of Mount Guye. It's a small clearing in a bamboo forest where, at midnight, the bright moon hangs directly above the sea of bamboo, offering a perfect view—hence the name.
"A small clearing in a bamboo forest? That sounds like a perfect place for an ambush."
The guest with a saber blurted out the punchline, instantly stripping the tea-written name of its storytelling fun. The sword-carrying guest's face fell, clearly displeased. The tea-brewing woman nearby chuckled, and the sword-carrying guest, saving face, didn't flare up, but continued his tale. Who hasn't heard of the market hidden in the bamboo sea? To get from Wulian Town to the market, one often passes through Moon-Reflecting. Once, there was a reckless bounty hunter who was hacked to death in that very clearing.
"But countless bounty hunters die bad deaths. Why did this one become the talk of the town?"
The saber-wielder finally hit the mark. The sword-wielder narrowed his eyes, looking meaningful. "Because this bounty hunter was a scapegoat, killed unjustly. Though there aren't many honest bounty hunters in the world, this one was upright. He had obtained a 'Cloud-Mist' weapon from Master Nan Hu Lai of the Casting Cloud Hut and was bringing it back to the market to deliver to his employer. The one who deserved to die was the employer."
At this, the surrounding tea guests grew interested, and the slow-moving tea-brewing woman picked up her fan, leaning in. Indeed, bounty hunters are in the business of doing dirty work for others; how did this one end up dying for someone else? Seeing listeners gathering from all sides, the sword-wielder's interest grew. He sat up straight, using his small teacup like a gavel.
"That bounty hunter was Lu Cang. Yes, no need to hide the name. Lu Cang was holding the sword case given by Nan Hu Lai, returning to the market at dusk, and stopped at Moon-Reflecting. Why did she stop? Ah, don't be impatient, we'll get to that later. Lu Cang leaned against a bamboo stalk, watching the setting sun and feeling the warm breeze, and couldn't help but let her thoughts wander: 'Great, great, that little girl can finally go back to Chang'an with her father.'"
"Wait a minute, you're not the person involved that day, how would you know what Lu Cang was thinking?"
The surrounding listeners chimed in, and the tea-brewing woman nodded thoughtfully. The sword-wielder hurriedly explained that he heard it from a colleague of Lu Cang, who knew why she took the job. The listeners' objections died down, and the sound of teacups tapping on the table resumed.
"Lu Cang was lost in the breeze when a rustling sound came from the bamboo forest. She thought it was just birds returning to their nests. But out of the forest stepped three warriors with sharp blades. On the left was the famous 'Thunder Sword' from Lychee Tower, on the right was the 'Wild Snow Saber' who shook the Cloudstep Arena, and the yellow-clad girl in the middle didn't look famous, but her clothes were clearly from the Casting Cloud Hut. It was obvious: Lu Cang had taken the 'Cloud-Mist' weapon from Nan Hu Lai, and they had come to pursue her."
"Wasn't that sword case given by Nan Hu Lai? Did he go back on his word?"
The sword-wielder perked up, leaning forward and speaking in a voice he couldn't suppress. "Lu Cang was puzzled too. The three newcomers stated their intent: Lu Cang had to leave behind the 'Cloud-Mist' weapon she had 'forcibly' obtained. Lu Cang sneered—she got it with her own skill, why should she return it? Instantly, swords were drawn, and the birds that had just returned to their nests were scared away."
"Didn't Lu Cang have the 'Cloud-Mist' weapon? Why didn't she pull it out and fight them?"
"Who's to say?"
He tapped his teacup, and the story took a sharp turn.
"Lu Cang saw there was no room for negotiation, so she opened the sword case. But the case—what about the case?—the case was empty! Empty? Nan Hu Lai gave her an empty case?"
The sword-wielder stopped talking, playfully fiddling with his teacup. The listeners discussed it heatedly, and the tea-brewing woman let out a giggle after listening for a while. A few sitting on the edge asked what she was laughing at, but she pursed her lips and didn't answer. Which bystander wouldn't find that scene laughable? The listeners debated for a long time and finally reached a consensus: this must have been Nan Hu Lai's brilliant plan.
"Indeed, it was Nan Hu Lai's brilliant plan, a chain of them. It's said that when Nan Hu Lai gave Lu Cang the case, he hinted for her to wait at Moon-Reflecting. No one knows what they agreed upon, but Lu Cang arrived as promised, and the pursuers followed. Lu Cang had been outplayed by Nan Hu Lai; she didn't get the weapon and was about to lose her life. The three attacked without a word. They fought in the bamboo forest from dusk until the stars filled the sky, and even Lu Cang's employer got dragged into it."
"Didn't the employer explain things clearly?"
The sword-wielder, dry-mouthed from talking about blades and shadows, took a sip of the freshly served tea to moisten his throat. "The employer didn't care about the life of a bounty hunter! Seeing them locked in a bloody battle, he snuck up, trying to steal the sword case in the chaos—he didn't know the case was empty! But the 'Wild Snow Saber' had already gone blood-crazy. He was known in the martial world for his 'Mad Demon' reputation and didn't bother to distinguish friend from foe, killing the 'thieving' employer with one strike."
"An undeserved disaster!"
"The bright moon hung in the sky. The three warriors collapsed from exhaustion, and Lu Cang was already a bloody mess, barely breathing. The three thought that despite the hard battle, it was over. But who would have thought there would be more movement in the forest! 'Thunder Sword' thought there was more support for the bounty hunter and tried to stand up with his sword, but stumbled after two steps, seeing a little girl of about eleven or twelve run out. 'Thunder Sword' was stunned and collapsed to the ground."
"Why was there a little girl? Where did she come from? Oh, wait, the employer's daughter! The little girl who should have been back in Chang'an!"
The sword-wielder was very satisfied; the listeners remembered the details. "The little girl ran over and saw her father was already dead, and Lu Cang would only last a moment longer. In her panic, she ran to Lu Cang, who handed her the blood-stained sword case and breathed her last. The three warriors were dumbfounded, and none of them stopped her. How could they? Hearing the little girl crying like rain, she had already explained most of the story. The three understood, and it was like a thunderbolt; they sat paralyzed on the ground, looking at each other. By the time they recovered, the girl was long gone, and the three could only take the sword case back to the Casting Cloud Hut."
The listeners' tea was refilled, and they patted the tables with sighs. Some praised Nan Hu Lai's plan, others lamented Lu Cang's injustice. After discussing for a while, they all became concerned about the whereabouts of the sword case. The sword-wielder shook his head. "Since then, the three warriors have vanished, and Nan Hu Lai's whereabouts are unknown. The sword case is likely lost, and this has long become an unsolved mystery in a corner of the martial world."
"Not necessarily."
The listeners looked toward the sound. The tea-brewing woman came over with a pot of fresh tea, refilling the sword-wielder's pot while speaking slowly. The sword-wielder was stunned, looking up at her.
"This story has been passed down with many inaccuracies. For instance, the three warriors didn't know the case was empty, so they weren't in cahoots with Nan Hu Lai, nor was it his clever plan. And the sword case—the little girl took it. The three warriors, knowing the truth, were heartbroken and didn't stop her. Presumably, she took it back to Chang'an."
"How do you know?"
The tea-brewing woman listened to the surrounding discussion without refuting it, only saying that she had brewed tea here for a long time and heard too many stories. Over time, she knew what was true and what was false. In this world, truth and falsehood are mixed; the listeners should just take it as a snack with their tea. "Also, when Lu Cang gave the sword case, she whispered one last thing to the little girl before she died."
"What were Lu Cang's last words?"
"She said, 'Follow the moon, go back to Chang'an, and grow up to be a great hero.'"
The listeners were silent for a long time, raising their teacups without knowing what to say. The tea stall went quiet, with only the sound of tea being poured. The owner of the tea stall returned from drying tea and saw the woman standing at the guest's table, thinking she was slacking off again.
"Cang Lu! Get back to boiling water!"
The woman smiled, turned, and disappeared into the tea stall's shed. Before long, the sword-wielder paid his bill and left, and the listeners gradually dispersed.

Lineage of the Casting Cloud Long Clan: Volume II Excerpt

The Legend of the Divine Sword is full of wonders. It has been told and retold so many times that it feels like a repetition, so today I shall present a new interpretation.
Centuries ago, master craftsmen gathered at the Casting Cloud Pavilion. Each had their own methods, and their forging techniques were as numerous as they were varied. Some quenched blades in cold springs, while others channeled fire into their swords. They argued endlessly, unable to agree.
It wasn't until the birth of the Long siblings that a turning point appeared. The brother was named Long Qi, and his sister, Long Nian. They were born with extraordinary signs. The siblings seemed to have a natural talent for craftsmanship; the moment they were born, their cries caused the furnace fires to flicker. They could manipulate the flames at will, shaping them into dancing dragons or swimming Kun. All who witnessed it were struck with awe.
One night, both dreamt of an old man with a white beard who descended from the clouds. The old man had the face of a child and eyes like stars. He carried a lantern that shone like the sun and a ruler as heavy as a mountain. In the dream, he taught them the immortal art of forging with fire, which is the foundation of today's "Cloud-Flow Quenching." After teaching them, the old man dissolved into clouds and vanished.
When the Long siblings awoke, they recounted their dreams to each other, and they matched perfectly. The room was filled with swirling clouds that would not dissipate, a sign of their destiny. The siblings summoned their closest friend to protect them. This friend was a Demonkin, eight feet tall, with a fierce face, wielding dual swords. He was so imposing that no one dared approach. The Demonkin swordsman rushed into the inner pavilion to retrieve the Cloud-Accumulation Stone that guarded the pavilion. While ordinary Cloud-Accumulation Stone is good material for forging, this stone contained a thousand years of cloud flow, a rarity unseen in centuries. No one had dared to use it for decades, and it was guarded by sixty-four craftsmen, yet no one dared to stop him.
As the Long siblings channeled the flow into the fire—the clouds from the sky and the flow from the earth—they converged in the furnace and attached to the stone. In an instant, the sound of hammers rang out like thunder, and the furnace temperature soared like the sun melting iron. Rainbow light streaked across the sky, and the sword's hum sounded like a dragon, triggering natural phenomena—dark clouds pressed down, lightning flashed, and a strange beast descended from the heavens, with a Tigerhead, lion's body, and snake's tail. What kind of weapon did the Long siblings forge to trigger such a trial?
The Demonkin swordsman showed no fear. With both swords drawn, he cut through the gale, slashed the lightning, and fought the beast alone.
The Tigerhead condensed wind into a hurricane, but the swordsman spun his blades to create his own, managing to Negate it. The snake's tail spat fire like a thousand arrows, but the swordsman endured the pain, pressed forward, and sliced off the tail. He spun his blades again, carving countless wounds into the lion's body, and finally stood atop the beast's neck, piercing the Tigerhead with both swords. His righteousness and courage left all who watched in awe.
Back at the furnace, the Long siblings did not falter. Long Qi focused on controlling the fire, while Long Nian focused on the hammer, both holding their positions with absolute concentration.
As Long Qi channeled the cloud flow into the furnace, he saw illusions: volcanoes erupting around the Casting Cloud Pavilion, flames swallowing the sky, and his fellow disciples trapped in a sea of fire, crying for help and begging him to extinguish the furnace. Sweat poured down Long Qi's forehead, but his mind remained steady. He thought, "This is a trial of the heart's fire. Ordinary fire is easy to control, but the heart's fire is hard to tame." He closed his eyes and focused, selecting the purest, most intense strand of fire from the thousands—a fire that does not burn external objects, but tempers the spirit. As that strand of heart's fire entered the furnace, it was the only fire capable of forging a Sanctified weapon.
On the other side, Long Nian struck the stone with her hammer, and with every blow, the earth shook. At first, it was a slight tremor, then it felt like a dragon turning beneath the earth. The forging table shook, the beams creaked, but Long Nian stood firm, her stance as solid as a rock. No matter how the world shook, her hammer strikes remained perfectly steady. Long Nian knew, "Though the external world changes, the heart's hammer must not move. One must become one with the hammer, using the spirit to forge the form." She shut out all distractions, pouring her entire spirit into the hammer. The hammer's shadow blurred, creating a rhythmic melody of metal and stone, ringing out like bells and chimes.
Suddenly, the world went silent, and all things stopped. The Long siblings emerged with their swords. Three divine swords were born: the first, Sky Dome, held by Long Qi; the second, Frost, held by Long Nian; and the third, End Times, gifted to their friend. The divine swords protected the pavilion, and the world marveled at them.
From then on, the Long lineage held control over the Casting Cloud, and the art of Cloud-Flow Quenching spread far and wide. Heroes from all directions came to seek them out in an endless stream. But where there is fortune, there is misfortune. Are these divine swords a blessing or a curse, and what kind of turmoil will they stir up? To know what happens next, stay tuned for the next chapter.

I have seen countless techniques in my life, but neither the power to shatter stone nor the speed of lightning can be called truly unparalleled.
The only one that amazed me was a technique called "Gale and Drizzle."
In this world, a gale is often accompanied by drizzle, for without the gale, the drizzle cannot drift far, and without the drizzle, people cannot see the shape of the gale.
The "Gale and Drizzle" I saw in my youth was, in fact, two people.
That winter came very early. The chill of early winter beat against all things through the firmament, and the branches were covered in crystalline frost. Azhao, as usual, supported A'ao as they walked along the mountain path back to their wooden house in the valley.
Although A'ao had not been in the North for long, she had stirred up a storm with her superb martial arts and uninhibited personality. She defeated major martial arts sects like the Pijin Sect, the Longwei Sect, and the Fengxuan School one after another, not only causing the masters to lose face but also bringing disgrace to the entire North.
People knew very little about Azhao, only that she was a herbalist who was inseparable from A'ao, and whenever A'ao was injured from a duel, Azhao would treat her.
Although they were close friends, their personalities were completely different. A'ao was fierce and competitive, determined to pursue the highest martial arts and defeat every master in the world, while Azhao preferred to heal all kinds of people and care for strange animals.
This time, A'ao was severely injured. It was a miracle she survived, but she ignored Azhao's advice and her own condition, insisting on participating in the duel the next day.
Neither of them knew that this duel was a conspiracy.
Major sects, long dissatisfied with the arrogant A'ao, had specifically issued a challenge, determined to take advantage of her injury to eliminate this threat once and for all.
No matter what, they would not let her leave the ring unscathed.
On the day of the duel, a light drizzle was falling. A'ao, wearing a bamboo hat and a black veil, stood in the arena before dawn.
"Fellow colleagues, I was too eager to win in the past and acted without restraint, causing offense. I am here today to apologize. I wonder if you could let go of our grievances..."
A'ao said in a low voice, asking everyone to cancel the duel.
Her tone left everyone confused. When had the arrogant A'ao ever been so humble?
"You say let it go, and we just let it go? Our master's injuries haven't even healed yet!"
"Exactly! You can't just call it off because you want to! Draw your sword!"
Major sects would never give up this opportunity.
Experts who had been lying in wait took turns to challenge her. Perhaps due to her injuries, A'ao could only parry that day, with no strength to fight back.
At noon, A'ao was exhausted and collapsed on the ring.
"Azhao!"
A piercing scream came from afar, and the real A'ao came running toward the ring.
It turned out that the "A'ao" in the ring was Azhao in disguise.
The sound of the drizzle was masked by A'ao's crying. Everyone looked at each other, not knowing how to handle the situation, and left one after another.
Before I left, I vaguely heard Azhao whisper.
"Come back to Jixia with me..."

Azhao died of her wounds, and A'ao disappeared without a trace.
Since then, no one has seen A'ao, including me, leaving only some half-true legends circulating.
That day, I was talking about this with my fellow disciples again.
Some said she fell ill from worry, some said she went elsewhere to start a new sect, and others said she abandoned her weapons and never touched martial arts again.
"It's just a pity. She was a talent, and her own martial path ended while she was still young," a senior brother sighed.
"I think her path didn't end; it had just begun."
We were too engrossed in our conversation to notice when the master appeared.
"It's going to rain again," the master said, looking at the dark clouds outside.
